subject: MAP: finalize hosting lane + geofence milestone and evaluation acceptance
body:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@brightlinehealth.com>
Cc: Asha Menon <asha.menon@brightlinehealth.com>
Date: Sat, 27 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: MAP: finalize hosting lane + geofence milestone and evaluation acceptance

Samir / Asha —

Thanks again for last week’s sync. Per our mutual action plan (attached v1.2), the one remaining gating decision before we lock pricing and the go-live window is which hosting lane you want to commit to for production and which region(s) we should reserve capacity in. High level options: Hosted (fastest, pay-as-you-go), Dedicated (reserved GPU pool, predictable latency/cost), Private (VPC/on-prem for PHI).

Quick ask: can you confirm a preferred lane for production (Hosted | Dedicated | Private) and the target region (us-east-1 or us-west-2) by EOD next Wednesday so we can lock the reserved capacity and legal timelines?

Notes for consideration:
- If you need PHI isolation starting day one, Private is the path — that adds procurement and an SOW milestone but we can do a phased approach (Private in core region + Hosted PoC).
- Dedicated gives you guaranteed throughput and faster scale but requires a 3–6 week capacity lead.
- Hosted is the quickest to start for the PoC and keeps costs variable while we finalize performance acceptance.

I’m looping in Karthik (SE) and Vanessa (Solutions) to propose a concise evaluation plan that ties to the MAP acceptance criteria and suggests a short ramp timeline. I attached the MAP, the SOC2 summary, and a draft SOW for legal to look at.

If easier, propose a 30-minute slot next week and we’ll align on the final lane and a binding milestone for procurement.

Best,
Rishi
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

---

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@brightlinehealth.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Asha Menon <asha.menon@brightlinehealth.com>, Brightline Health Legal <legal@brightlinehealth.com>
Date: Sat, 27 Feb 2027 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MAP: finalize hosting lane + geofence milestone and evaluation acceptance

Thanks Rishi — good summary. Short answers for now:

- Production target: Dedicated for long-term (we need predictable latency for clinical workflows).
- PoC: We are comfortable starting the PoC on Hosted to accelerate validation and integration with our FE. We expect to flip to Dedicated for production after the PoC acceptance.
- Region: Prefer us-east-1 for proximity to our primary data stores and lower egress costs.

Constraints / asks from our side:
- If PHI is in scope for the PoC (some test datasets will include synthetic PHI-like tokens), we need strong data handling guarantees — if Private is required for regulatory reasons, we might have to take the Private lane. Let me check with legal and confirm by Wed.
- Can you provide the short list of acceptance tests tied to latency/throughput we discussed so I can confirm infra sizing with infra ops?

I’ll aim to confirm lane by Wed EOD. Appreciate the MAP — please flag the exact dates we need to commit to for capacity reservations so we can align procurement.

—Samir
Director of Product | Brightline Health

---

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 28 Feb 2027 08:31:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: MAP: finalize hosting lane + geofence milestone and evaluation acceptance

Team — forwarding Samir’s reply. He’s leaning Dedicated for prod, Hosted for PoC, region us-east-1, but legal may push Private depending on PHI. Can we tighten up the MAP with a clear PO/commitment date and a concise evaluation plan (latency/throughput metrics, sample prompts, dataset slices) that we can hand to their infra and legal?

Immediate asks:
- Karthik: draft a 1-page evaluation acceptance checklist (3–5 metrics + pass thresholds) and note any capacity lead time if we reserve Dedicated GPUs for 10k qps-equivalent requests per hour.
- Vanessa: update the MAP milestones with procurement dates and a fallback plan (Hosted->Dedicated migration path + timelines).
- Laura: please pre-fill the SOW draft with the services milestones and start/end dates once we have a firm commit date.

We’ll send the edited MAP back to Samir and Asha so they can accept inline and trigger legal. Goal: get a signed SOW and committed Dedicated capacity within 3 weeks after lane confirmation.

Thanks —
Rishi

---

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: MAP: finalize hosting lane + geofence milestone and evaluation acceptance

Rishi —

Attached below is a compact evaluation plan you can paste into the MAP. Key points:

Evaluation acceptance (PoC -> Dedicated cutover) — proposed 2-week PoC window
- Latency: P50 < 120ms, P95 < 350ms for typical 1k-token prompts under our batching profile.
- Throughput: sustain 1,200 reqs/min with concurrency profile (burst-handling up to 2,500 reqs/min for 10 minutes).
- Quality: synthetic prompt set (200 prompts) with > 92% functional parity vs reference outputs (we’ll provide the eval harness).
- Stability: no >5% error rate over a 24-hour window during the acceptance run.

Capacity lead / region notes:
- us-east-1: we have spare Dedicated slots but to guarantee capacity we need a written commit 14 business days prior to expected cutover.
- us-west-2: similar but slightly longer lead (18 business days) for GPU reservation.

Quick config recs for PoC on Hosted:
- Use continuous batching, 8k token cache window, quantization profile Q4 for the fastest latencies during PoC.
- Instrument token-level tracing and sample logging (PII scrub) so we can validate performance and quality.

I’ll attach a short shell script to run stress tests (stub) and the eval harness pointers.

—Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

---

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 14:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: MAP: finalize hosting lane + geofence milestone and evaluation acceptance

Adding the MAP milestone strip below and procurement dates. I made conservative estimates so Brightline has slack:

MAP milestones (updated)
- Wed 2027-03-03: Brightline confirms hosting lane (Hosted | Dedicated | Private) and target region — acceptance by inline reply to MAP v1.2.
- Fri 2027-03-10: Redwood provides final SOW draft and firm capacity reservation window.
- Mon 2027-03-20 -> Fri 2027-04-02: 2-week PoC window (if Hosted) or dry-run (if Dedicated in reserved staging).
- Mon 2027-04-05: Cutover planning — data handling checklist completed, legal redlines closed.
- Mon 2027-04-12: Target production launch on Dedicated (assuming commit by 03/03).

Procurement notes:
- For Dedicated reservation we’ll issue a capacity quote that requires a signed order form 10 business days prior to cutover; that enables us to pin GPUs in us-east-1.
- If legal requires Private because of PHI, we’ll add the Private SOW addendum; expect an extra 3–4 weeks for network & infra provisioning.

Laura — please keep the SOW placeholders for order form dates. Karthik — we need the eval checklist in the MAP before I send to Samir.

—Vanessa
Head of Solutions | Redwood Inference

---

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@brightlinehealth.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 3 Mar 2027 09:30:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: MAP: finalize hosting lane + geofence milestone and evaluation acceptance

Appreciate the clarity — we will commit to Dedicated for production and start the PoC on Hosted (us-east-1). Confirming by the 03/03 milestone here.

Next items from our side:
- Legal will send redlines to the SOW draft (expect by 03/05). They will also confirm whether Private is mandatory for any PHI elements; I suspect we can proceed with Hosted PoC if we pseudonymize the test set — legal will confirm.
- Procurement needs the capacity quote and order form to start internal approvals. Can you get the capacity quote and the order form stub by 03/10 (per MAP)?

We accept the evaluation acceptance criteria Karthik proposed — please add the formal checklist to the MAP and we’ll run the validation with infra ops during the PoC.

—Samir

---

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@brightlinehealth.com>, Asha Menon <asha.menon@brightlinehealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Brightline Health Legal <legal@brightlinehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Mar 2027 16:05:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: MAP: finalize hosting lane + geofence milestone and evaluation acceptance

Samir / Asha — great, thanks for the confirmation and for accepting the proposed acceptance criteria. Action items / next steps from Redwood: 

- Today (03/03): Update MAP_Brightline_v1.2.xlsx with Karthik’s checklist and Vanessa’s milestones (attached).
- By 03/05: Redwood to upload final SOW draft (SOW_Brightline_draft.docx) to the Box link and notify legal.
- By 03/10: Capacity quote and order form stub to Brightline procurement.
- PoC window: 03/20 -> 04/02 (Hosted in us-east-1). We will support stress runs and provide the eval harness with pass/fail reporting.

Attachments included: MAP_Brightline_v1.2.xlsx, SOC2_summary_2026.pdf (summary), SOW_Brightline_draft.docx (placeholder). I’ll also add the HubSpot deal link to the MAP.

If legal flags Private or additional controls we will move the Private addendum into the SOW — I have a Solutions/Eng workstream ready to scope network requirements.

Thanks — we’ll send the updated MAP link in a follow-up shortly.

Best,
Rishi

[Attachments: MAP_Brightline_v1.2.xlsx; SOC2_summary_2026.pdf (stub); SOW_Brightline_draft.docx]
